result.summary: Block dispatch: the retry design can silently mark an unrecovered transcript as processed and erase its quarantine warning.

findings.title: Deleting the quarantine record can suppress the promised retry
findings.body: Table A1 assumes the no-record path always selects the file, but ledger.js:261–262 returns skip-processed when mtimeMs <= baseline_mtime. This is reachable when a previously recorded path is restored with an older timestamp: its changed fingerprint permits parsing, which can then quarantine it as parse-threw. Reproduced with baseline 2000 and restored mtime 1000: the specified deletion changes skip-quarantined to skip-processed. The hardened parser never runs, and removing the record also removes the warning.
findings.recommendation: Replace deletion with durable retryable state that bypasses the baseline, such as the existing deferred selection semantics, while retaining the one-shot gate. Update the contract and require an upgrade test with a matching quarantine fingerprint and mtime at or below the baseline, including a ledger round-trip.

next_steps: Revise the retry contract and its mirrored constraints before implementation.
